Acorn Squash.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low nitrogen once fruiting.
Acorn Squash.harvest_cues: Skin resists fingernail scratch; stem begins to dry and cork over.
Acorn Squash.tip: Unlike larger squash, best harvested small (under 2 lb) for sweetest flesh.

Amaranth.tip: Dual-purpose: harvest young leaves as greens, or let mature for grain seed heads.
Amaranth.harvest_cues: Young leaves any time; grain when seed heads dry and seeds fall easily.
Amaranth.storage: Fresh leaves: fridge 3 days. Grain: sealed container, cool and dry, up to 1 year.

Aronia.harvest_cues: Clusters of dark purple-black berries in late summer; taste before picking.
Aronia.tip: Extremely cold-hardy; tolerates wet soils. High in antioxidants.

Arugula.tip: Bolts quickly in heat; succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest.
Arugula.harvest_cues: Leaves 2-3 inches; harvest before flowering for mildest flavor.
Arugula.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; keep dry.

Asparagus.tip: Plant 1- or 2-year crowns; don't harvest first 2 years to build root strength.
Asparagus.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced spring + phosphorus after harvest season.
Asparagus.harvest_cues: Spears 6-8 inches, pencil-thick; snap at base. Harvest 2-4 weeks (young bed).
Asparagus.storage: Fridge upright in water up to 5 days.

Avocados.tip: Zones 9-11 only — protect from frost when young.

Basil.tip: Pinch flowers to keep leaves coming.
Basil.fertilizer: Light balanced; avoid high nitrogen (reduces flavor).
Basil.harvest_cues: Pinch above leaf node; harvest before flowering.
Basil.storage: Store in water on counter 1 week; freeze in oil for long term.

Bay Leaf.tip: Slow-growing shrub; harvest outer leaves year-round. Can be kept in a large pot and brought indoors in cold climates.
Bay Leaf.germ_temp: 70°F (slow from seed — propagate from cuttings instead)
Bay Leaf.fertilizer: Light balanced feed in spring; very low maintenance.
Bay Leaf.harvest_cues: Pick mature dark-green leaves. Dry for 2 weeks for stronger flavour.
Bay Leaf.storage: Fresh: fridge 1-2 weeks. Dried: airtight jar 1 year+.

Beans.tip: Do not start indoors — direct sow only.
Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); light phosphorus at planting.
Beans.harvest_cues: Pods firm and filled out; snap cleanly.
Beans.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze for longer.

Beets.tip: Each 'seed' is a cluster — thin to 3-4 in after sprouting.
Beets.harvest_cues: Roots 1.5-3 inches diameter; greens edible at any size.
Beets.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; remove tops.

Bitter Melon.tip: Start indoors 4 weeks before last frost. Soak seeds 24 hours first to aid germination. Provide a trellis — vines climb vigorously to 15 ft.
Bitter Melon.fertilizer: Compost-rich soil plus balanced liquid feed every 2 weeks during fruiting.
Bitter Melon.harvest_cues: Harvest young when skin is still bright green and firm — about 4–6 in long. Overripe fruit turns orange.
Bitter Melon.storage: Refrigerate unwrapped up to 1 week. Slice and blanch to freeze up to 3 months.

Black-eyed Peas.fertilizer: Minimal — nitrogen-fixing; inoculate seeds for best yield.
Black-eyed Peas.harvest_cues: Pick green pods at 60–70 days; for dry beans wait until pods are papery.
Black-eyed Peas.storage: Fresh: fridge 3–5 days. Dried: cool dry place 1 year+.
Black-eyed Peas.tip: Thrives in heat and poor soil where other legumes struggle. Perfect for summer gaps.

Blackberries.tip: Thornless varieties (Loch Ness, Chester) are much easier to manage in home gardens. Train canes along wires.
Blackberries.fertilizer: Balanced spring feed; mulch thickly to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
Blackberries.harvest_cues: Fully black and comes away from the plug easily; flesh soft and deeply sweet.
Blackberries.storage: Fridge 3-4 days; freeze immediately if not eating fresh.

Blackcurrants.days: 3 years to full production; harvest Jul-Aug
Blackcurrants.tip: Prune out old wood each autumn — fruiting is best on 1-year-old stems. Extremely high in vitamin C.
Blackcurrants.fertilizer: High nitrogen in spring; top-dress with compost every autumn.
Blackcurrants.harvest_cues: Whole strig (cluster) dark black and slightly soft. Taste-test before harvest.
Blackcurrants.storage: Fridge 3-4 days. Freeze whole on trays then bag — lasts 12 months.

Blueberries.tip: Blueberries demand acidic soil (pH 4.5–5.5). Grow in ericaceous compost or amend heavily with sulphur and bark mulch.
Blueberries.fertilizer: Ericaceous (acidic) fertilizer each spring; no lime ever.
Blueberries.harvest_cues: Fully blue with slight grey bloom; taste test — ripe berries are sweet, not tart.
Blueberries.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze for long-term storage.

Bok Choy.tip: Quick cool-season crop; bolt-resistant varieties extend harvest.
Bok Choy.harvest_cues: Leaves full and crisp; cut at base before bolting.
Bok Choy.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; keeps best unwashed.

Borage.tip: Self-seeds prolifically — deadhead if you don't want it everywhere next year. Blue star flowers are edible; freeze in ice cubes for drinks.
Borage.fertilizer: Unfussy — thrives with minimal feeding. Rich soil reduces flowering.
Borage.harvest_cues: Harvest individual star-shaped flowers when fully open; young leaves are edible before stems become hairy.
Borage.storage: Use flowers immediately; freeze in ice cubes to preserve. Leaves wilt quickly — use same day.

Borlotti Beans.tip: Italian shelling bean; harvest fresh (flageolet stage) or dry for storing.
Borlotti Beans.harvest_cues: Fresh: pods mottled pink/cream, swollen but not dried. Dry: pods papery brown.
Borlotti Beans.storage: Fresh: fridge 3 days. Dried: airtight container up to 1 year.

Boysenberry.fertilizer: Balanced fertiliser in spring; add potassium for fruit quality.
Boysenberry.harvest_cues: Berries are deep purple-maroon and come off the cane with gentle pulling.
Boysenberry.tip: Trailing canes need a trellis; prune old canes after fruiting in autumn.

Broad Beans.tip: Cool-season crop; sow in autumn or very early spring. Pinch out growing tips to deter blackfly.
Broad Beans.fertilizer: Minimal; fixes own nitrogen. Light phosphorus at planting.
Broad Beans.harvest_cues: Pods plump and firm, 3-5 in; beans inside soft and green.
Broad Beans.storage: Shell and refrigerate up to 3 days; blanch and freeze for long term.

Broccoli.tip: Harvest before florets start to open.
Broccoli.harvest_cues: Head tight and dark green; cut before florets open.
Broccoli.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze.

Broccoli Rabe.tip: Harvest before flower buds open for best flavour. Slightly bitter — blanch before sautéing to mellow.
Broccoli Rabe.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; balanced fertilizer at planting.
Broccoli Rabe.harvest_cues: Cut central shoot with flower buds still tight. Side shoots follow for weeks.
Broccoli Rabe.storage: Fridge 3-5 days. Blanch and freeze well.

Brussels Sprouts.tip: Start early for fall harvest; flavor improves after frost.
Brussels Sprouts.fertilizer: High nitrogen; side-dress monthly, reduce once heads form.
Brussels Sprouts.harvest_cues: Sprouts firm and 1-2 inches; harvest from bottom up as they mature.
Brussels Sprouts.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze.

Butternut Squash.tip: Leave on vine until skin is tan and stem has dried; cures off vine for 2 weeks.
Butternut Squash.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; compost at planting and side-dress monthly.
Butternut Squash.harvest_cues: Skin tan and hard; stem dry and corky.
Butternut Squash.storage: Cool, dry place up to 3-6 months.

Cabbage.tip: Even moisture prevents heads from splitting.
Cabbage.harvest_cues: Head firm and dense; squeeze — it should feel solid.
Cabbage.storage: Fridge up to 2 months; don't wash until use.

Calendula.tip: Deadhead constantly to extend flowering season well into autumn. The more you pick, the more it blooms.
Calendula.fertilizer: Light; too much nitrogen reduces flowers.
Calendula.harvest_cues: Petals fully open in morning sun; bright orange or yellow. Pick regularly to encourage more blooms.
Calendula.storage: Dry petals on a screen in a cool airy place; store in an airtight jar for months.

Cardoon.fertilizer: High nitrogen and potassium; heavy feeder.
Cardoon.harvest_cues: Blanch stalks by tying together for 3-4 weeks; harvest when tender and pale.
Cardoon.storage: Use fresh; stores 1 week in fridge.
Cardoon.tip: Blanch stems to reduce bitterness before harvest. A dramatic, architectural plant.

Carrots.tip: Loose, deep soil is essential — thin to avoid forking.
Carrots.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; moderate phosphorus and potassium.
Carrots.harvest_cues: Shoulders visible at soil surface; orange and firm.
Carrots.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; remove tops first.

Cauliflower.tip: Tie outer leaves over the head to blanch it white.
Cauliflower.harvest_cues: Head 6-8 inches, compact and white; cut before curds separate.
Cauliflower.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze.

Cavolo Nero.fertilizer: High nitrogen; top-dress with compost mid-season.
Cavolo Nero.harvest_cues: Pick lower leaves when dark green and about 10 in long.
Cavolo Nero.tip: Frost improves flavour. Harvest outer leaves and the plant keeps growing.

Celeriac.tip: Start indoors 10-12 weeks early; needs long cool season and consistent moisture.
Celeriac.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; high nitrogen throughout season.
Celeriac.harvest_cues: Root 3-4 inches across; firm and aromatic. Flavor peaks after light frost.
Celeriac.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; stores well in cool cellar.

Celery.tip: Needs consistently moist soil — mulch heavily.
Celery.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; high nitrogen throughout season.
Celery.harvest_cues: Stalks 8+ inches; cut outer stalks first or harvest whole.
Celery.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; wrap in foil to prevent drying.

Celtuce.fertilizer: Light balanced; nitrogen for leaf growth.
Celtuce.harvest_cues: Stem reaches 12-18 in; peel and eat stem raw or cooked. Leaves are also edible.
Celtuce.tip: Bolt-tolerant; can grow through summer heat when regular lettuce fails.

Chamomile.tip: Press seeds onto soil surface — they need light to germinate. Pinch early blooms to encourage bushier growth.
Chamomile.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen; excess fertility reduces flower production.
Chamomile.harvest_cues: Harvest flowers when fully open, petals reflexed back — snap off individually.
Chamomile.storage: Dry flowers on a screen in a warm place; store in an airtight jar up to 1 year.

Chard.tip: Cut outer leaves and the plant keeps producing.
Chard.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 6-8 inches; cut at base.
Chard.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; stems and leaves store separately.

Cherry Tomatoes.tip: Indeterminate varieties need staking; pinch suckers for bigger fruit.
Cherry Tomatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Cherry Tomatoes.harvest_cues: Fully coloured; squeeze gently — should give slightly.
Cherry Tomatoes.storage: Counter at room temp; use within 5 days.

Chervil.tip: Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous supply. Bolts quickly in heat — grow in spring, autumn, and under cover in winter.
Chervil.fertilizer: Minimal — light soil with some compost is ideal.
Chervil.harvest_cues: Cut outer leaves before flowering; leaves have a delicate anise flavour and wilt quickly after cutting.
Chervil.storage: Use fresh immediately; fridge 2 days max. Freezes acceptably in ice cubes.

Chia.tip: Direct sow after all frost danger has passed and the soil is warm. Chia needs a long hot season of 4–5 months to produce mature seed. Thin to 12 in.
Chia.fertilizer: Minimal; grows well in average, well-drained soil.
Chia.harvest_cues: Harvest seed heads when bracts turn grey-brown and seeds fall when tapped. Cut whole spikes, bag, and dry.
Chia.storage: Dried seeds keep up to 4 years in an airtight container.

Chickpeas.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); avoid heavy feeding.
Chickpeas.harvest_cues: Pods turn tan and begin to rattle; plant starts to dry out.
Chickpeas.storage: Dry beans store 2+ years in a cool, dark place.
Chickpeas.tip: Needs hot, dry conditions to ripen; avoid waterlogged soils.

Chicory.tip: For witloof/Belgian endive: dig roots in autumn, pot in moist sand indoors, and 'force' in darkness for crisp, pale chicons in winter.
Chicory.fertilizer: Moderate; balanced fertiliser at sowing, then minimal feeding.
Chicory.harvest_cues: Cut leaves young for salads; dig roots in autumn for forcing. Forced chicons are ready in 3–4 weeks.
Chicory.storage: Fresh leaves use immediately. Forced chicons refrigerate up to 2 weeks. Dried roots grind into coffee substitute.

Chives.tip: Perennial in zones 3+; divide clumps every 3 years to reinvigorate.
Chives.harvest_cues: Snip leaves 2-3 inches from base; harvest before flowering.
Chives.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; freeze chopped for long term.

Chrysanthemum Greens.harvest_cues: Harvest outer leaves at 4–6 in or cut entire plant 1 in above soil to regrow.
Chrysanthemum Greens.tip: Cool-season crop that bolts in heat; direct sow in spring and again in late summer.

Cilantro.tip: Bolts quickly — succession sow every 3 weeks. The dried seed is coriander.
Cilantro.harvest_cues: Leaves ferny and 6+ inches; harvest before flowering.
Cilantro.storage: Fridge in water up to 1 week; freeze packed in oil.

Citrus.tip: In zones below 9b grow in a large pot and move under cover when frost threatens. Lemons and limes fruit almost year-round; oranges and mandarins fruit in winter.
Citrus.fertilizer: Citrus-specific slow-release fertiliser 3× per year; iron/manganese trace minerals if leaves yellow.
Citrus.harvest_cues: Colour change is the main cue; taste-test to confirm sweetness. Fruit won't continue ripening off the tree.
Citrus.storage: Store at room temperature 1 week or refrigerate up to 4 weeks.

Collard Greens.tip: More heat-tolerant than kale; harvest outer leaves for continuous production.
Collard Greens.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 8-10 inches; pick lower leaves first.
Collard Greens.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze.

Comfrey.tip: Plant root cuttings 2 in deep. Chop-and-drop leaves as a free fertiliser mulch — very high in potassium and nitrogen.
Comfrey.fertilizer: Self-fertilising via deep taproots; rarely needs feeding.
Comfrey.harvest_cues: Cut leaves at ground level when plants reach 24 in. Repeat 3–4 times per season.
Comfrey.storage: Use fresh as liquid feed (steep in water 4 weeks) or dry for herbal use.

Corn.tip: Plant in blocks of 4+ rows for good pollination.
Corn.fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; side-dress at knee height.
Corn.harvest_cues: Silks brown and dry; kernels plump and milky when punctured.
Corn.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; eat as soon as possible for best flavor.

Cress.tip: One of the fastest crops you can grow — ready from sowing in 10–14 days on a sunny windowsill or direct in the garden. Sow thickly and cut with scissors.
Cress.fertilizer: No feeding needed for such a short crop.
Cress.harvest_cues: Cut when seedlings reach 2–3 in, leaving roots for a second (smaller) cut.
Cress.storage: Best eaten immediately. Store cut cress in water in the fridge up to 2 days.

Cucumbers.tip: Trellis vining types to save space.
Cucumbers.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen when vining.
Cucumbers.harvest_cues: Dark green and firm; pick before yellowing.
Cucumbers.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; do not freeze.

Daikon.tip: Excellent soil loosener — deep taproot breaks up compacted ground. Direct sow only; hates transplanting.
Daikon.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; high phosphorus/potassium for root development.
Daikon.harvest_cues: Shoulder visible at soil surface, 2-3 in diameter. Pull before extreme cold splits roots.
Daikon.storage: Fridge 2-3 weeks. Pickles excellently (Japanese tsukemono style).

Delicata Squash.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low nitrogen once flowering.
Delicata Squash.harvest_cues: Cream-and-green stripes fully formed; stem dry and corky.
Delicata Squash.storage: Cool dry place up to 3 months; thin skin means shorter shelf life than other squash.
Delicata Squash.tip: Skin is tender enough to eat; no need to peel. One of the sweetest winter squashes.

Dill.tip: Direct sow — dislikes transplanting. Succession sow for continuous harvest.
Dill.harvest_cues: Harvest leaves before flowering; seeds when heads turn brown.
Dill.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; dry or freeze for long term.

Echinacea.tip: Cold-stratify seeds for 4–8 weeks before sowing. First-year plants rarely bloom; roots are harvestable after 3 years.
Echinacea.fertilizer: Minimal; thrives in average to lean soil. Avoid high nitrogen.
Echinacea.harvest_cues: Cut flowers just as petals begin to droop. Harvest roots in autumn of year 3 or 4.
Echinacea.storage: Dry flowers/roots at low heat; store in airtight jars up to 2 years.

Edamame.tip: Harvest at the green stage before pods dry — pick when plump and bright.
Edamame.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); balanced at planting.
Edamame.harvest_cues: Pods plump and bright green, 3 inches long; beans visible through pod.
Edamame.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; blanch and freeze for longer.

Eggplant.tip: Needs warm soil — wait until nights stay above 55°F.
Eggplant.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen mid-season.
Eggplant.harvest_cues: Skin glossy and slightly springy; don't let it go dull.
Eggplant.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; best used fresh.

Elderberries.tip: Plant two varieties for best fruiting. Prune old canes each spring. Never eat raw berries — they must be cooked first.
Elderberries.fertilizer: Apply balanced slow-release in spring; topdress with compost annually.
Elderberries.harvest_cues: Harvest full clusters when berries are deep purple-black and just starting to droop. Leaves and unripe berries are toxic.
Elderberries.storage: Freeze or cook into syrup, juice, or jam. Dried berries keep up to 1 year.

Endive.tip: Cover heads for 2 weeks before harvest to blanch and mellow the flavor.
Endive.harvest_cues: Head firm and full; blanch if desired before cutting.
Endive.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; one of the longest-storing salad greens.

Epazote.fertilizer: Minimal — grows well in poor to average soil.
Epazote.harvest_cues: Harvest stems and leaves anytime once 8 in tall. Use young leaves for cooking.
Epazote.storage: Fridge 3–5 days; dries and freezes well.
Epazote.tip: Essential in Mexican black bean cooking — reduces flatulence and adds distinctive flavour. Self-seeds prolifically.

Fava Beans.tip: Cool-season legume — direct sow 4-6 weeks before last frost; tolerates light frost.
Fava Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); light phosphorus at planting.
Fava Beans.harvest_cues: Pods fat and filled; beans inside clear with no dark ring.
Fava Beans.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; shell and freeze for longer.

Fennel.tip: Grow in isolation — allelopathic to most vegetables. Keep away from all food crops.
Fennel.fertilizer: Light balanced; too much fertility reduces flavor.
Fennel.harvest_cues: Bulb 3-5 inches across; fronds harvestable anytime before bolting.
Fennel.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; fronds dry well.

Figs.tip: In colder zones (6b-7a) grow in a pot and overwinter under cover. Prune lightly to encourage the 'breba' early crop on old wood.
Figs.fertilizer: Feed with balanced fertiliser monthly in summer; avoid excess nitrogen which delays fruiting.
Figs.harvest_cues: Ripe figs droop, skin softens, and a drop of nectar may appear at the eye. Pick gently — they bruise easily.
Figs.storage: Best eaten fresh the same day. Refrigerate up to 2 days; dry or jam for longer storage.

Flaxseed.tip: Direct sow thickly in cool soil in spring or early autumn. Beautiful blue flowers precede the seed heads. Grow in large blocks for wind pollination.
Flaxseed.fertilizer: Minimal; over-feeding produces straw with few seeds.
Flaxseed.harvest_cues: Harvest seed heads when 90% of stems have turned golden-brown and pods rattle. Pull whole plants and dry in bundles.
Flaxseed.storage: Dried seeds keep up to 1 year at room temperature, or 2 years refrigerated.

Gai Lan.fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich; side-dress with compost at midseason.
Gai Lan.harvest_cues: Cut stems with flower buds still closed; harvest when 8-10 in tall.
Gai Lan.tip: More heat tolerant than Western broccoli; succession-sow every 3 weeks for continuous harvest.

Galangal.fertilizer: Balanced slow-release; top-dress with compost monthly.
Galangal.harvest_cues: Rhizomes mature when plant yellows in autumn; harvest as needed.
Galangal.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; freeze sliced rhizomes.
Galangal.tip: Needs tropical warmth; grow in pots indoors in cool climates.

Garlic.tip: Plant cloves in fall, pointy end up.
Garlic.fertilizer: Nitrogen in spring; stop fertilizing by early summer.
Garlic.harvest_cues: Bottom 3-4 leaves brown; dig before all leaves die back.
Garlic.storage: Cure 3-4 weeks in warm, dry place; store up to 6 months.

Ginger.tip: Zones 8b+ outdoor; elsewhere start in pots and bring indoors before frost.
Ginger.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and die back in fall; dig after first frost threat.
Ginger.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; freeze grated; dry and grind.

Globe Artichoke.tip: Perennial zones 7+; in cold zones start early indoors and treat as annual.
Globe Artichoke.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced monthly during growing season.
Globe Artichoke.harvest_cues: Buds before they open; tight scales and firm; cut 1-2 inches below head.

Goji Berries.fertilizer: Balanced fertiliser in spring; avoid excess nitrogen.
Goji Berries.harvest_cues: Berries are bright red and come off the stem cleanly without squishing.
Goji Berries.storage: Fresh 1-2 weeks in fridge; dry for long-term storage.
Goji Berries.tip: Tolerates drought once established; train as a hedge or on trellis.

Good King Henry.tip: Perennial; don't harvest heavily in first year. Leaves used like spinach, shoots like asparagus.
Good King Henry.harvest_cues: Young leaves and shoots in spring; cut shoots when 4-6 in, leaves anytime.

Gooseberries.tip: Prune into an open-centred 'goblet' shape each winter to maximise airflow and reduce mildew. Wear thick gloves!
Gooseberries.fertilizer: Balanced NPK in early spring; sulphate of potash in midsummer.
Gooseberries.harvest_cues: For cooking: firm and green. For dessert: fully ripe (yellow, red or white), slightly soft with bloom.
Gooseberries.storage: Fridge 1 week; freeze or jam for long-term.

Grapes.tip: Plant bare-root vines in early spring. Train along a wire trellis. Annual winter pruning (leaving 2 buds per spur) is essential for productive fruit spurs.
Grapes.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; excess causes lush vines with little fruit. Apply compost annually.
Grapes.harvest_cues: Taste test is the best guide — sugar develops in the last weeks. Colour change alone is not reliable.
Grapes.storage: Keep unwashed in refrigerator up to 3 weeks. Freeze, juice, or make wine/jam.

Green Onions.tip: Snip from above — plants regrow; succession sow for continuous harvest.
Green Onions.harvest_cues: Stems pencil-thick; harvest at any size.
Green Onions.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; stand in water to keep fresh.

Ground Cherries.tip: Fruit falls to ground when ripe — fallen fruit inside husk is ready.
Ground Cherries.harvest_cues: Fruit falls to ground; papery husk tan. Check frequently.
Ground Cherries.storage: In husk at room temp 2-3 weeks; fridge in husk 1-2 months.

Hamburg Parsley.tip: Grown for its parsnip-like root and parsley-flavoured leaves — dual-purpose.
Hamburg Parsley.fertilizer: Light balanced; heavy nitrogen favours leaves over roots.
Hamburg Parsley.harvest_cues: Roots 4-6 in long; harvest after light frost for sweetness.
Hamburg Parsley.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; root stores in sand up to 3 months.

Honeyberry.fertilizer: Balanced spring dressing; avoid high nitrogen.
Honeyberry.harvest_cues: Berries turn deep blue-purple and are slightly soft; taste-test before full harvest.
Honeyberry.storage: Fridge 1 week; freeze up to 12 months.
Honeyberry.tip: Needs 2 different varieties for pollination. Extremely cold-hardy — survives -40°F / -40°C.

Hops.tip: Plant rhizomes in spring. Vigorous climbers reaching 20 ft — provide a sturdy trellis. Harvest in late summer when cones are papery and fragrant.
Hops.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; apply compost in spring and a balanced feed at bud formation.
Hops.harvest_cues: Harvest cone clusters when they turn light green/gold, feel dry and papery, and smell strongly hoppy.
Hops.storage: Dry at 120°F for 8–10 hours; vacuum-seal and freeze for up to 1 year.

Horseradish.tip: Plant root pieces in spring; very vigorous — give it dedicated space.
Horseradish.fertilizer: Minimal; top-dress with compost each spring.
Horseradish.harvest_cues: Harvest roots after first frost for best flavor; dig in fall.
Horseradish.storage: Fridge up to 3 months; grate fresh for maximum pungency.

Hyacinth Beans.harvest_cues: Flat pods are bright purple or white; pick before seeds visibly bulge.
Hyacinth Beans.storage: Use fresh; must be well-cooked before eating.
Hyacinth Beans.tip: Must cook thoroughly — raw beans contain toxic compounds. A beautiful ornamental vine.

Jalapeño.tip: Stress slightly by withholding water near harvest to increase heat.
Jalapeño.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; reduce nitrogen once flowering.
Jalapeño.harvest_cues: Deep green; about 3 inches long. Red when fully ripe and hotter.
Jalapeño.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze or pickle for long term.

Jerusalem Artichoke.tip: Invasive — plant in a contained bed or large pot to control spread.
Jerusalem Artichoke.harvest_cues: Stalks die back in fall; dig tubers through winter.
Jerusalem Artichoke.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; leave in ground as living pantry.

Kabocha Squash.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; potassium boost at fruiting.
Kabocha Squash.harvest_cues: Skin turns dark green/orange-green; stem fully corked and dry.
Kabocha Squash.tip: Cures better than most squash — leave 2 weeks at room temperature after harvest to improve flavour.

Kale.tip: Flavor improves after a light frost.
Kale.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 8-10 inches; pick lower leaves first.
Kale.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; remove stems before storing.

Kiwi.tip: Hardy kiwi (Actinidia arguta) fruits reliably to zone 4. Plant one male vine for every 6–8 female vines. Provide a very sturdy trellis — vines can live 50 years.
Kiwi.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen in spring; avoid feeding after midsummer to harden new growth.
Kiwi.harvest_cues: Hardy kiwi fruits are ripe when they yield slightly to pressure and taste sweet. Pick before frost.
Kiwi.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 weeks. Ripen at room temperature if picked slightly early.

Kohlrabi.tip: Harvest when bulb is tennis ball size — larger gets woody.
Kohlrabi.harvest_cues: Bulb 2-3 inches diameter; firm and bright.
Kohlrabi.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; store bulb and leaves separately.

Komatsuna.fertilizer: Light nitrogen; compost-rich soil is sufficient.
Komatsuna.harvest_cues: Harvest baby leaves from 20 days; mature heads at 4–6 weeks.
Komatsuna.tip: Extremely cold-hardy — survives light frost and even mild snow. Great for winter growing.

Lavender.days: Blooms in year 2 from seed; year 1 from cutting
Lavender.tip: Excellent bee attractor and companion plant. Trim after flowering to prevent woody growth. Edible flowers.
Lavender.fertilizer: Very low; excess nitrogen reduces fragrance. Sandy, well-drained soil preferred.
Lavender.harvest_cues: Cut flower spikes when about 1/3 of buds are open for best fragrance.
Lavender.storage: Dry bunches upside-down for 2-4 weeks. Store dried in airtight container.

Leeks.tip: Blanch by hilling soil up around stems as they grow.
Leeks.harvest_cues: Shaft 1 inch diameter; blanched white portion 4+ inches.
Leeks.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; or leave in ground until needed.

Lemon Balm.days: 75-90 days to mature plant (harvest lightly first year)
Lemon Balm.tip: Contain it in a pot if you don't want it spreading — it's very vigorous. Cut back hard after flowering to refresh growth.
Lemon Balm.fertilizer: Minimal — thrives in average soil; over-feeding reduces essential oil potency.
Lemon Balm.harvest_cues: Harvest young leaves before flowering for best lemon scent; cut stems in the morning.
Lemon Balm.storage: Dry leaves in a dark airy place 1-2 weeks; store in airtight jars. Or freeze in ice cubes.

Lemon Verbena.tip: Tender perennial; overwinter indoors in cold climates. Intensely lemony scent.
Lemon Verbena.harvest_cues: Snip leafy stems anytime; most aromatic before flowering.
Lemon Verbena.storage: Dry in bundles or freeze in water. Dried keeps 1 year.

Lemongrass.tip: Zones 8b+ perennial; root a grocery store stalk in water to start for free.
Lemongrass.harvest_cues: Stalks 1 foot or taller; cut at base; inner stalk white-pale yellow.
Lemongrass.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; dry or freeze stalks.

Lentils.harvest_cues: Lower pods turn tan and rattle; harvest before pods shatter.
Lentils.storage: Dried lentils store 2+ years in airtight container.
Lentils.tip: Cool-season crop; sow as soon as soil can be worked in spring.

Lettuce.tip: Bolts in heat — succession sow every 2 weeks.
Lettuce.harvest_cues: Outer leaves firm and full; cut before bolting.
Lettuce.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; keep moist.

Lima Beans.tip: Don't plant until soil is 65°F — cold soil causes poor germination. Dry beans store for years.
Lima Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; compost at planting. Avoid high nitrogen which favours leaves over pods.
Lima Beans.harvest_cues: Green stage: pods plump and green. Dry stage: pods papery and rattling.
Lima Beans.storage: Fresh: fridge 3-5 days. Dried: airtight jar 2+ years.

Loganberry.fertilizer: Balanced fertiliser in spring; add potassium for fruit quality.
Loganberry.harvest_cues: Large dark-red berries with slightly tart flavour; harvest before they soften.
Loganberry.tip: Trailing canes need a trellis; remove old canes after harvest.

Lovage.tip: Vigorous perennial reaching 6 ft; use sparingly — very strong celery flavour.
Lovage.harvest_cues: Young leaves in spring; stems and seeds in summer. Cut back hard to encourage regrowth.
Lovage.storage: Fresh fridge 3 days; dry or freeze for long term.

Luffa.tip: Soak seeds overnight before sowing. Needs a long hot season — start indoors 4–6 weeks early. Provide a strong vertical trellis for 10+ ft vines.
Luffa.fertilizer: Regular balanced feeding throughout the long growing season.
Luffa.harvest_cues: For eating: harvest 4–6 in long (smooth, firm). For sponges: leave until the skin turns brown and the gourd rattles when shaken.
Luffa.storage: Eating-size luffa: refrigerate 1 week. Dry sponge luffa: peel, bleach, and store indefinitely.

Malabar Spinach.fertilizer: High nitrogen for lush leaf growth.
Malabar Spinach.harvest_cues: Harvest young leaves and stem tips; continual picking extends season.
Malabar Spinach.tip: Thrives in hot, humid conditions; grows vigorously on a trellis.

Mangetout.tip: Flat edible-pod pea; harvest before peas swell. Needs support or trellis.
Mangetout.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; light balanced at planting.
Mangetout.harvest_cues: Pods flat, 3-4 in, before peas bulge. Pick every 2-3 days.
Mangetout.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze.

Mangoes.fertilizer: Balanced fertilizer 3-4x per year; reduce nitrogen once mature.

Marigolds.tip: Plant throughout the vegetable garden — marigold root secretions deter nematodes and the scent confuses many pests.
Marigolds.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; fertiliser encourages foliage at expense of flowers.
Marigolds.harvest_cues: Deadhead spent blooms to prolong flowering; harvest whole heads for seed when dry and brown.
Marigolds.storage: Dried petals keep 6 months in an airtight container. Collect seeds from dried heads.

Marjoram.tip: Harvest before flowering for best flavour; treat as annual in cold climates.
Marjoram.harvest_cues: Snip stems once plant is 6 in tall; just before bud break for strongest flavour.
Marjoram.storage: Dry in bunches or freeze. Dried keeps 1-2 years.

Medlar.fertilizer: Light balanced spring dressing; rarely needs feeding once established.
Medlar.harvest_cues: Harvest after first frost in November. Store (blet) for 3–4 weeks until skin darkens and flesh softens.
Medlar.storage: Blet in a cool place for 3–4 weeks before eating. Do not eat hard.
Medlar.tip: Must 'blet' (partially rot) before eating — traditional British autumn fruit. Ornamental year-round. Self-fertile.

Melons.tip: Needs long warm season — start indoors in cool climates.
Melons.fertilizer: Balanced early; switch to low-nitrogen when fruit sets.
Melons.harvest_cues: Sweet smell at stem end; slips off vine with light pressure.
Melons.storage: Counter until ripe; fridge once cut.

Microgreens.tip: Grow in shallow trays; harvest with scissors just above the soil line.
Microgreens.fertilizer: None needed — use quality potting mix.
Microgreens.harvest_cues: First true leaves emerging; typically 1-3 inches tall.
Microgreens.storage: Fridge up to 7 days; keep dry.

Mint.tip: Contain in pots — spreads aggressively by underground runners.
Mint.fertilizer: Light; vigorous grower needs minimal feeding.
Mint.harvest_cues: Leaves 3-4 inches; harvest before flowering for best flavor.
Mint.storage: Fridge in water up to 1 week; dry or freeze.

Mitsuba.fertilizer: Light nitrogen; keep soil consistently moist.
Mitsuba.harvest_cues: Harvest outer leaves from 8 weeks; cut and come again.
Mitsuba.storage: Fridge 3–4 days; stems in water like cut herbs.
Mitsuba.tip: One of few vegetables that prefers shade — ideal for underplanting taller crops. Slightly celery-like flavour.

Mizuna.tip: Bolt-resistant for a brassica; ideal for cut-and-come-again harvesting.
Mizuna.harvest_cues: Leaves 4-6 in; cut outer leaves or whole plant at base.
Mizuna.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; keep unwashed.

Mulberry.tip: Fast-growing once established. Fruit stains everything — plant away from paths and use a tarp at harvest. Birds love them too, so netting helps.
Mulberry.fertilizer: Low fertility; self-sufficient once mature. Light compost mulch annually.
Mulberry.harvest_cues: Berries are ripe when deep purple-black (red varieties when fully red) and drop easily. Shake branches over a tarp.
Mulberry.storage: Very perishable — eat within 1–2 days or freeze immediately. Also makes excellent jam.

Mung Beans.harvest_cues: Harvest pods when green for fresh use; allow to yellow for sprouts or dry beans.
Mung Beans.storage: Fresh: fridge 3 days. Dried: cool dry place 1 year+.
Mung Beans.tip: Can also be sprouted indoors year-round in a jar — no garden space needed for sprouts.

Mustard Greens.tip: Very fast cool-season crop; sow in fall for mildest flavor.
Mustard Greens.fertilizer: Light nitrogen; quick crop needs minimal feeding.
Mustard Greens.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; best used fresh.

Mâche.tip: Cold-hardy to 5°F — an excellent winter green in cold frames.
Mâche.harvest_cues: Rosettes 3-4 inches across; harvest whole or leaf by leaf.
Mâche.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; very delicate.

Napa Cabbage.tip: Cool-season crop; bolts in summer heat. Best for spring and autumn. Ideal for kimchi and stir-fries.
Napa Cabbage.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen throughout; balanced fertilizer every 3 weeks.
Napa Cabbage.harvest_cues: Head firm and full, outer leaves wrap tightly. Squeeze — it should feel dense.
Napa Cabbage.storage: Fridge 1-2 months. Core removed, wrapped in damp paper.

Nasturtium.tip: Grow in poor soil for maximum flowers — rich soil produces mainly leaves. Both flowers and leaves are peppery and edible.
Nasturtium.fertilizer: Minimal — avoid nitrogen-rich feeds or you get leaves but few flowers.
pests: Aphids (act as trap crop — draw aphids away from vegetables)
Nasturtium.harvest_cues: Flowers open fully; pick in the morning for best flavour. Leaves anytime. Seeds when fat and green for capers.
Nasturtium.storage: Use flowers same day. Seeds pickle as 'poor man's capers' in brine.

New Zealand Spinach.harvest_cues: Pick young tip shoots; plant produces continuously through heat.
New Zealand Spinach.tip: Soak seeds 24 hrs before planting; excellent heat-tolerant spinach substitute.
New Zealand Spinach.water: Moderate; more drought-tolerant than true spinach

Okra.tip: Soak seeds overnight to speed germination.
Okra.harvest_cues: Pods 2-4 inches; pick every 2 days to prevent toughening.
Okra.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; slice and freeze long term.

Onions.tip: Stop watering when tops fall over to cure bulbs.
Onions.fertilizer: High nitrogen early; reduce once bulbing starts.
Onions.harvest_cues: Tops fall over naturally; cure in sun 1-2 weeks.
Onions.storage: Cool, dry, dark place up to 6 months after curing.

Orach.harvest_cues: Pick young leaves; remove flower spikes to prolong the harvest season.
Orach.tip: More heat-tolerant than spinach; bolt-resistant and self-seeds readily.

Oregano.tip: Perennial zones 5+; slightly stressed plants have stronger flavor.
Oregano.fertilizer: Very light; lean soil improves flavor.
Oregano.harvest_cues: Harvest stems before flowering; cut back by 1/3 maximum.
Oregano.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries excellently.

Padron Peppers.fertilizer: Balanced; high phosphorus at transplant; potassium when fruiting.
Padron Peppers.harvest_cues: Pick small at 1-2 in for mild; allow to grow for more heat.
Padron Peppers.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; pan-fry with sea salt.
Padron Peppers.tip: Pick small for milder flavour; some turn spicy when larger like Shishito.

Pak Choi.tip: Similar to Bok Choy; harvest baby size at 30 days or full heads at 45.
Pak Choi.harvest_cues: Leaves full and crisp; cut at base before bolting.

Parsley.tip: Soak seed overnight to speed germination; biennial — best leaf production in year 1.
Parsley.harvest_cues: Stems with 3 leaf segments; harvest outer stems first.
Parsley.storage: Fridge in water up to 2 weeks; dry or freeze for long term.

Parsnips.tip: Sow fresh seed; flavor peaks after frost. Slow to germinate — be patient.
Parsnips.fertilizer: Moderate balanced; avoid excess nitrogen (causes forking).
Parsnips.harvest_cues: Roots 8-12 inches; sweetest after a hard frost.
Parsnips.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; or leave in ground under mulch.

Passionfruit.tip: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before last frost. Provide a trellis immediately — vines grow rapidly. Flowers are self-fertile but benefit from hand-pollinating.
Passionfruit.fertilizer: High potassium feed every 4 weeks during fruiting. Avoid excess nitrogen.
Passionfruit.harvest_cues: Fruit falls to the ground when ripe. Wrinkled purple/yellow skin means peak ripeness.
Passionfruit.storage: Store at room temperature up to 1 week; refrigerate up to 3 weeks. Freeze pulp up to 12 months.

Pattypan Squash.fertilizer: High nitrogen early; switch to potassium when flowering.
Pattypan Squash.harvest_cues: Harvest at 2-4 in diameter; skin should yield to a fingernail.
Pattypan Squash.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; eat fresh.
Pattypan Squash.tip: Harvest frequently to keep plant producing; small fruits are most tender.

Peanuts.tip: Zones 6b+ for reliable harvest; hill soil as plants flower — pods develop underground.
Peanuts.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); high calcium helps pod fill.
Peanuts.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow; dig and check a pod — inner hull ridged and full.
Peanuts.storage: Dry in shell 2-3 weeks, then cure; store months in cool dry place.

Peas.tip: Direct sow as soon as soil can be worked in spring.
Peas.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; light phosphorus at planting.
Peas.harvest_cues: Pods plump and filled; pick daily to encourage production.
Peas.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze for longer.

Peppers.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; reduce nitrogen when fruiting.
Peppers.harvest_cues: Green or wait until fully colored; firm and glossy.
Peppers.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze for long term.

Potatoes.tip: Hill soil as vines grow to increase yield; stop watering when tops die back.
Potatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress when plants are 6 inches tall.
Potatoes.harvest_cues: Skin set (doesn't rub off easily); dig after tops die back.
Potatoes.storage: Cool, dark, dry place 2-3 months; cure 1 week at 55°F first.

Pumpkins.tip: Each plant needs 50+ sq ft — plan space accordingly.
Pumpkins.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced at planting, low-nitrogen once flowering.
Pumpkins.harvest_cues: Deep color and hard rind; stem dry and corky.
Pumpkins.storage: Cool, dry place 2-3 months; do not freeze.

Purple Sprouting Broccoli.fertilizer: High nitrogen in autumn; balanced spring dressing.
Purple Sprouting Broccoli.harvest_cues: Cut purple spears before flowers open; side shoots follow for weeks.
Purple Sprouting Broccoli.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze up to 12 months.
Purple Sprouting Broccoli.tip: Sow May–June for late-winter harvest. One of the few crops that bridges the hungry gap.

Purslane.tip: High in omega-3s; thrives in heat and poor soil where others struggle.
Purslane.fertilizer: None needed; thrives in poor soil.
Purslane.harvest_cues: Snip succulent stems and leaves once 4-6 in tall.
Purslane.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; best eaten fresh.

Quince.fertilizer: Low-moderate nitrogen in early spring; avoid high nitrogen.
Quince.harvest_cues: Fruit turns yellow and fragrant in October-November; still firm when ripe.
Quince.storage: Cool dark place 2–3 months; improves with time. Don't store near apples.
Quince.tip: Too astringent to eat raw but outstanding cooked. Self-fertile; plant in a sheltered spot.

Quinoa.tip: Needs cool growing seasons; bolts in high heat. Rinse seed heads well — removes saponins.
Quinoa.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen at planting; light once established.
Quinoa.harvest_cues: Seed heads dry and papery; seeds release easily when rubbed.
Quinoa.storage: Dried grain in airtight container up to 2 years.

Radicchio.tip: Sow in midsummer for a late autumn harvest — cool weather develops the best colour and flavour. Cut back summer sowings and the stumps will resprout.
Radicchio.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; consistent moisture prevents bitterness.
Radicchio.harvest_cues: Harvest firm, tight heads when they reach tennis-ball size and the colour is deep red-purple.
Radicchio.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 weeks. Lightly braising or grilling mellows the bitterness.

Radishes.tip: Fastest crop in the garden — great row markers.
Radishes.harvest_cues: Roots 1 inch diameter; pull before getting pithy.
Radishes.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; remove tops.

Raspberries.tip: Summer-fruiting canes: cut spent floricanes to ground after harvest. Autumn canes: cut all to ground in late winter.
Raspberries.fertilizer: Balanced feed in early spring; avoid high nitrogen after midsummer.
Raspberries.harvest_cues: Berries come away easily from the plug; deep colour throughout; sweet aroma.
Raspberries.storage: Fridge 2-3 days; freeze on trays then bag for up to 12 months.

Redcurrants.tip: Redcurrants fruit on old wood — don't remove old branches indiscriminately. They're more shade-tolerant than other soft fruit.
Redcurrants.fertilizer: Balanced spring feed + high-potash summer feed for best colour and flavour.
Redcurrants.harvest_cues: Whole trusses turn deep red simultaneously; taste test a few berries for balanced sweet-tart flavour.
Redcurrants.storage: Fridge up to 1 week on the truss; freeze whole truss for later.

Rhubarb.tip: Don't harvest first year; NEVER eat the leaves — they are toxic.
Rhubarb.fertilizer: Balanced in spring; compost mulch annually.
Rhubarb.harvest_cues: Stalks 12-18 inches; pull and twist — never cut more than 1/3 of plant.
Rhubarb.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; chops and freezes well.

Romanesco.fertilizer: High nitrogen; consistent feeding for large heads.
Romanesco.harvest_cues: Spiralled chartreuse head fully formed but still tight; harvest before any yellowing.
Romanesco.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; or blanch and freeze.
Romanesco.tip: Needs very consistent moisture — any stress causes loose, irregular heads.

Rosemary.tip: Perennial zones 7+; grow in pots elsewhere and overwinter indoors.
Rosemary.fertilizer: Very light; excess fertilizer reduces flavor and fragrance.
Rosemary.harvest_cues: Snip tips 3-4 inches; harvest before or just after flowering.
Rosemary.storage: Fridge 2 weeks; dry bundles or freeze for long term.

Runner Beans.tip: Provide a 6–8 ft trellis. Pick regularly to keep pods coming — leaving mature pods stops production.
Runner Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); compost at planting + potassium during flowering.
Runner Beans.harvest_cues: Pods 6-8 in long, before seeds visibly bulge. Check every 2 days in peak season.
Runner Beans.storage: Fridge 4-5 days; blanch and freeze up to 12 months.

Rutabaga.tip: Direct sow early summer for fall harvest; frost improves sweetness.
Rutabaga.harvest_cues: Roots 3-5 inches; harvest after first frost for best flavor.
Rutabaga.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; root cellar several months.

Saffron.tip: Plant corms in late summer; they bloom in autumn. Each flower has only 3 stigmas — harvest them by hand in the morning on the day they open.
Saffron.fertilizer: Low-phosphorus balanced fertiliser in early spring. Corms multiply over years.
Saffron.harvest_cues: Harvest vivid red stigmas from freshly opened flowers on dry mornings. Dry on paper at low heat for 15 minutes.
Saffron.storage: Dried saffron keeps 2–3 years in an airtight container away from light.

Sage.tip: Perennial zones 4+; prune hard in spring to prevent woodiness.
Sage.fertilizer: Very light; excess fertility reduces flavor.
Sage.harvest_cues: Harvest leaves before or just after flowering.
Sage.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries and freezes well.

Salsify.tip: Deep, loose soil essential for straight roots. Frost improves flavour.
Salsify.harvest_cues: Roots 8-10 in long, pencil-thick; dig after first frost for sweetness.
Salsify.storage: Store in sand in cool dark place up to 4 months.

Savory.tip: Summer savory is annual; winter savory is perennial and hardier.
Savory.harvest_cues: Snip young stems before flowering; harvest lightly the first year for perennial types.
Savory.storage: Dry or freeze; dried keeps 1-2 years.

Scorzonera.fertilizer: Low; avoid fresh manure which causes forking.
Scorzonera.harvest_cues: Roots reach 1 in diameter; can be left in ground over winter.
Scorzonera.storage: Leave in ground until needed; fridge up to 2 weeks.
Scorzonera.tip: Use fresh seed only; old seed germinates poorly. Needs deep, stone-free soil.

Sea Buckthorn.harvest_cues: Bright orange berry clusters in fall; harvest before hard frost.
Sea Buckthorn.storage: Freeze berries; excellent for juice and jam.
Sea Buckthorn.tip: Plant one male for every 6 female shrubs to ensure fruiting. Extremely cold-hardy.

Shallots.tip: Plant sets in fall (mild climates) or early spring (cold climates).
Shallots.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; reduce once bulbing starts.
Shallots.harvest_cues: Tops fall and yellow; cure 2-3 weeks in warm dry spot.
Shallots.storage: Cool, dry, dark place up to 6 months after curing.

Shishito Peppers.fertilizer: Balanced; high phosphorus at transplant; potassium when fruiting.
Shishito Peppers.harvest_cues: Pick at 3-4 in, bright green; harvest frequently to encourage production.
Shishito Peppers.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; best eaten blistered and fresh.
Shishito Peppers.tip: About 1 in 10 peppers is spicy — the variety's famous quirk!

Shiso.tip: Self-seeds readily; both green and red varieties are edible. Popular in Japanese cuisine.
Shiso.harvest_cues: Leaves 4-6 in; harvest before flowering for best flavour.
Shiso.storage: Wrap in damp paper towel, fridge up to 5 days.

Snow Peas.tip: Harvest while flat — the flat edible pod is the goal, not the pea inside. Trellis at 4-6 ft.
Snow Peas.fertilizer: Minimal; compost at planting, no extra nitrogen needed.
Snow Peas.harvest_cues: Flat pod, seeds barely visible through skin. Pick before pods swell.
Snow Peas.storage: Fridge 3-5 days. Stir-fry or blanch and freeze.

Sorrel.tip: Remove flower stalks promptly to keep leaf production going. Leaves are sour — use like spinach to add acidity to soups and sauces.
Sorrel.fertilizer: Light nitrogen once in spring; low-maintenance perennial.
Sorrel.harvest_cues: Pick outer leaves when 4-6 inches long. Leaves are ready all season if flower stalks are removed.
Sorrel.storage: Fridge 3-5 days; blanch and freeze for long-term use in soups.

Spaghetti Squash.fertilizer: High nitrogen early; switch to potassium when flowering.
Spaghetti Squash.harvest_cues: Skin is yellow and hard; vine is dying back; stem is corky.
Spaghetti Squash.storage: Cool dry place up to 3 months.
Spaghetti Squash.tip: A winter squash; allow full maturity on the vine before harvesting.

Spinach.tip: Cool-season crop — sow in early spring or fall.
Spinach.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; side-dress lightly once established.
Spinach.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 3+ inches; harvest before heat causes bolting.
Spinach.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; do not wash until use.

Squash.tip: Direct sow after last frost — transplants poorly.
Squash.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; side-dress monthly with balanced fertilizer.
Squash.harvest_cues: Skin resists thumbnail scratch; rich color.
Squash.storage: Cool, dry place up to 3 months (winter squash); fridge 5 days (summer).

Stevia.tip: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Leaves are 30-40x sweeter than sugar.
Stevia.harvest_cues: Harvest leaves before flowering for maximum sweetness; cut stems 1/3.
Stevia.storage: Fresh leaves fridge 5 days; dry and store in airtight container up to 1 year.

Strawberries.tip: Remove first-year flowers on June-bearing types for stronger plants.
Strawberries.fertilizer: Balanced in spring; high phosphorus supports fruiting.
Strawberries.harvest_cues: Fully red all over; slight give; stem snaps cleanly.
Strawberries.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; do not wash until use. Freeze whole.

Sugar Snap Peas.tip: Eat pods whole — no shelling needed. Sow as soon as soil can be worked; peas love cool weather.
Sugar Snap Peas.fertilizer: Minimal — fix own nitrogen. Top-dress compost at sowing.
Sugar Snap Peas.harvest_cues: Pod plump and rounded but still bright green. Crisp snap when bent.
Sugar Snap Peas.storage: Fridge 5-7 days; best eaten same day. Blanch and freeze well.

Sunflowers.tip: Excellent trap crop for aphids. Edible seeds — harvest when back of head turns brown and dry. Attracts pollinators.
Sunflowers.fertilizer: Low to moderate; high nitrogen causes leafy growth with fewer seeds.
Sunflowers.harvest_cues: Back of head turns yellow-brown, seeds firm and striped. Cover with netting to deter birds.
Sunflowers.storage: Dry seeds on head for 2-3 weeks. Shell and store in airtight container 1 year.

Sweet Cicely.harvest_cues: Harvest fresh leaves spring through summer. Leaves taste anise-sweet.
Sweet Cicely.tip: Perennial herb that dies back in winter. Seed needs cold stratification — sow in autumn outdoors. Sweetens tart fruits naturally.

Sweet Corn.tip: Plant in blocks of 4+ rows for wind pollination; don't grow near field corn.
Sweet Corn.fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; side-dress at knee height.
Sweet Corn.harvest_cues: Silks brown; kernels plump and milky when pierced.
Sweet Corn.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; eat immediately for best sweetness.

Sweet Peas.tip: Primarily ornamental; some varieties have edible young pods. Deadhead frequently to prolong bloom.
Sweet Peas.fertilizer: High potassium for flowering; low nitrogen.
Sweet Peas.harvest_cues: Pick flowers as they open; do not allow seed pods to develop if you want continuous bloom.
Sweet Peas.storage: Flowers last 5 days in water; seeds dried and stored cool.

Sweet Potatoes.tip: Plant slips, not seeds — cure dug roots for 2 weeks.
Sweet Potatoes.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; high potassium at planting.
Sweet Potatoes.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and vines die back; skin doesn't rub off.
Sweet Potatoes.storage: Cure 10-14 days at 85°F; store at 55-60°F up to 6 months.

Taro.tip: Plant corms in warm, moist soil once all frost risk has passed. Taro thrives in waterlogged or consistently moist conditions. Leaves are also edible when cooked.
Taro.fertilizer: High nitrogen and potassium; top-dress with balanced fertiliser monthly.
Taro.harvest_cues: Harvest when leaves start to yellow and die back, indicating corms have reached full size (7–9 months).
Taro.storage: Cure in a warm, dry place 5–7 days, then store in a cool, dry location up to 2 months.

Tarragon.depth: Transplant or division (French variety doesn't set viable seed)
Tarragon.tip: Always grow French (not Russian) tarragon — Russian has little flavour. French tarragon must be grown from cuttings or division, not seed.
Tarragon.fertilizer: Light; excellent in poor, well-drained soil.
Tarragon.harvest_cues: Harvest young shoot tips 3-4 inches long before plant flowers; leaves most flavourful in late spring.
Tarragon.storage: Dry or freeze in ice cubes; makes excellent tarragon vinegar.

Tatsoi.tip: Very cold-hardy; can survive light frosts. Rosette form makes it decorative.
Tatsoi.harvest_cues: Rosette full and compact; harvest outer leaves or whole at base.

Thai Basil.fertilizer: Balanced; avoid excess nitrogen which reduces flavour.
Thai Basil.harvest_cues: Pinch stems just above a leaf pair; harvest before flowering for best flavour.
Thai Basil.storage: Fridge 1-2 weeks; freeze or blend into pesto.
Thai Basil.tip: More heat-tolerant and slower to bolt than sweet basil; purple flowers are edible.

Thyme.tip: Perennial zones 5+; excellent ground cover between larger plants.
Thyme.fertilizer: Very light; well-drained soil matters more than fertility.
Thyme.harvest_cues: Harvest leafy stems anytime; just before flowering is strongest.
Thyme.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries excellently.

Tiger Nuts.fertilizer: Balanced NPK at planting; potassium at mid-season.
Tiger Nuts.harvest_cues: Dig after foliage yellows; tubers should be firm and sweet.
Tiger Nuts.storage: Dry for 2–4 weeks; then cool dry place up to 12 months.
Tiger Nuts.tip: Technically a sedge grass. Nutty, sweet tubers — base of Spanish horchata. Invasive if allowed to spread.

Tomatillos.tip: Need 2 plants for pollination; papery husk bursts when ripe.
Tomatillos.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Tomatillos.harvest_cues: Husk fills out fully and starts to split or brown; fruit firm inside.
Tomatillos.storage: Counter in husk 1-2 weeks; fridge up to 3 weeks.

Tomatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Tomatoes.harvest_cues: Fully colored and slightly soft; twist to test.
Tomatoes.storage: Counter at room temp; use within 1 week.

Turmeric.tip: Similar to ginger — long season tropical. Start rhizomes indoors 8 weeks early in cool zones.
Turmeric.fertilizer: Monthly balanced; high potassium before harvest.
Turmeric.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and drop in fall; rhizomes bright orange when scraped.
Turmeric.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; dry and grind; freeze.

Turnips.tip: Thin early for best root development; greens are edible and nutritious.
Turnips.harvest_cues: Roots 2-3 inches; younger is more tender.
Turnips.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; cool cellar up to a month.

Valerian.tip: Sow on the soil surface — needs light to germinate. Roots are harvestable in autumn of year 2. Cats are attracted to the plant.
Valerian.harvest_cues: Harvest roots in autumn of year 2 when dormant; flowers are harvested just before peak bloom.
Valerian.storage: Dry roots at low temperature; store in airtight containers up to 2 years.

Vietnamese Coriander.fertilizer: Light balanced feed; grows vigorously with minimal inputs.
Vietnamese Coriander.harvest_cues: Harvest stems and leaves anytime once established; cut above a node to encourage bushing.
Vietnamese Coriander.storage: Fridge in water like cut flowers, up to 1 week; or freeze.
Vietnamese Coriander.tip: Unlike cilantro, doesn't bolt in heat — use as a warm-season coriander substitute. Frost tender; bring indoors in winter.

Viola.fertilizer: Light balanced feed; over-feeding reduces flowers.
Viola.harvest_cues: Pick fully open flowers in the morning for best flavour and colour.
Viola.storage: Use same day; or press between damp paper and refrigerate overnight.
Viola.tip: All parts above ground are edible. Cool-season; flowers prolifically in spring and autumn.

Water Chestnut.harvest_cues: Corms form after plants die back in autumn; harvest by hand.
Water Chestnut.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze peeled corms.
Water Chestnut.tip: Grow in a tub of water at least 6 in deep; needs a long, warm growing season.
Water Chestnut.water: Aquatic; keep in 2-4 in of standing water

Watercress.tip: Needs consistently moist or flowing water; excellent in containers with wet saucers.
Watercress.fertilizer: Light; grows well in nutrient-rich water.
Watercress.harvest_cues: Stems 6-8 inches; harvest tips to encourage bushiness.
Watercress.storage: Fridge in water up to 5 days.

Watermelon.tip: Needs long, hot summers (90+ frost-free days). Thump the fruit — a hollow sound means it's ripe.
Watermelon.fertilizer: High nitrogen at planting, switch to phosphorus/potassium once vines run.
Watermelon.harvest_cues: Yellowed ground spot, dried tendril nearest fruit, hollow thump.
Watermelon.storage: Whole: room temp 2 weeks. Cut: fridge 3-5 days.

Yacon.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; potassium-rich at tuber development.
Yacon.harvest_cues: Harvest after first light frost kills foliage. Tubers continue sweetening after harvest.
Yacon.storage: Leave 1–2 weeks in sun to increase sweetness; then cool dark place up to 3 months.
Yacon.tip: Tubers taste like sweet apple-pear when cured. Leaves make a sweet herbal tea. Frost tender.

Yardlong Beans.tip: Needs trellis or tall support (6-8 ft). Thrives in heat — ideal summer crop.
Yardlong Beans.harvest_cues: Pods 12-18 in, still tender; harvest every 2-3 days to encourage production.

Yarrow.tip: Drought-tolerant once established. Spreads freely — divide clumps every 2–3 years to keep tidy. Excellent pollinator plant.
Yarrow.fertilizer: Thrives without feeding; rich soil causes floppy growth.
Yarrow.harvest_cues: Cut flower heads when 2/3 open for fresh use or when fully open for drying.
Yarrow.storage: Hang upside down in bunches to dry; keeps up to 2 years dried.

Zucchini.tip: Pick when 6-8 inches for best flavour; plants produce rapidly in peak season.
Zucchini.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen mid-season.
Zucchini.harvest_cues: 6-8 inches long; skin tender and easily pierced.
Zucchini.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; best eaten fresh.
